frames.label: The idea
frames.title: Sid wanted a café of his own.
frames.body: This busy café lane looked like a promising place.
frames.description: A close view of a busy café lane. Sid’s vacant blue-awning unit sits between operating cafés.

frames.label: The assumption
frames.title: The cafés next door were busy.
frames.body: Surely there was room for one more?
frames.description: A closer view of the same vacant unit, highlighted between its busy café neighbors.

frames.label: The doubt
frames.title: But what was bringing people here?
frames.body: The metro explained some of the crowd. It didn’t tell Sid who would buy.
frames.description: The view widens from Sid’s café lane to the shared parking, crossing and nearby underground metro entrance.

frames.label: The context
frames.title: He needed more than footfall.
frames.body: Who lives and works nearby? What do they spend? What do the existing cafés already offer?
frames.description: The full neighborhood reveals residential towers, offices, the metro and café lane. People, spending and competition are questions about this whole area.

frames.label: The response
frames.title: Same lane. A clearer picture.
frames.body: GeoMarketeer helps businesses understand a neighborhood before choosing where to open.
frames.description: The same full neighborhood, with Sid’s original vacant unit gently emphasized. No different location or business outcome is shown.
